+    layout = fakes.packed_zigzag_layout((4096, 2048, 2048), 1, 0, 5, device="cuda")
+    sq = layout[0].numel()
+    q, k, w = _inputs(sq, sq, seed=13, signed_weights=True)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(5)
+    query = torch.randn((sq, 1, 64, 576), generator=generator, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    key = torch.randn((sq, 1, 1, 576), generator=generator, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+    real = dsa_cudnn_kernels._indexer_topk_bshd
+    seen = {}
+
+    def recording(*args, **kwargs):
+        seen["selection"] = real(*args, **kwargs)
+        return seen["selection"]
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_indexer_topk_bshd", recording)
+    mxfp8 = _sparse_loss(q, k, w, query, key, layout, 1, 0, _K, "mxfp8")
+    indices, lengths, _payload = seen["selection"]
+    valid = torch.arange(_K, device="cuda").view(1, 1, -1) < lengths.unsqueeze(-1)
+    bf16_payload = torch.gather(_dense_reference(q, k, w), 1, indices[0].clamp(min=0).long())
+    bf16_payload = bf16_payload.unsqueeze(0).masked_fill(~valid, torch.finfo(torch.float32).min)
+
+    def same_selection(*_args, **_kwargs):
+        return indices.clone(), lengths.clone(), bf16_payload.clone()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_indexer_topk_bshd", same_selection)
+    bf16 = _sparse_loss(q, k, w, query, key, layout, 1, 0, _K, "bf16")
+    rel = ((mxfp8[0] - bf16[0]).abs() / bf16[0].abs()).item()
+    print(
+        f"[mxfp8-loss-same-selection] mxfp8 {mxfp8[0].item():.6e} bf16 {bf16[0].item():.6e} rel {rel:.2e}"
+    )
+    assert rel <= 1e-5
+    for name, grad_mxfp8, grad_bf16 in zip("qkw", mxfp8[1:], bf16[1:]):
+        cosine = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(
+            grad_mxfp8.float().flatten(), grad_bf16.float().flatten(), dim=0
+        ).item()
+        print(f"[mxfp8-loss-same-selection] grad {name} cosine {cosine:.8f}")
+        assert cosine > 1 - 1e-5

+"""Loading the cuDNN frontend DSA namespace must not pin the caller's tensors.
+
+``cudnn.DSA`` imports the kernel modules behind an entry point on first attribute access.
+CUTLASS DSL 4.6 kernel decorators keep ``inspect.currentframe()`` in a local, so every
+decoration leaves a self-referencing frame whose ``f_back`` chain reaches the frame that
+triggered the import. With automatic GC disabled (``--manual-gc``), a first access from
+inside a training step therefore held that step's activations until the next explicit
+collection. These CPU tests model that frontend and check that MCore resolves every entry
+point in one call and leaves nothing of the caller alive.
+"""
+
+import gc
+import inspect
+import re
+import sys
+import types
+import weakref
+
+import pytest
+
+from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant import dsa_cudnn_kernels
+
+
+def _decorate_like_cutlass_dsl_4_6():
+    """Mimic ``CuTeDSL.kernel`` of CUTLASS DSL 4.6: keep the own frame in a local."""
+    cur_frame = inspect.currentframe()
+    frame = cur_frame.f_back
+    return frame.f_lineno
+
+
+class _LazyDSANamespace:
+    """``cudnn.DSA`` stand-in: imports (decorates) an entry point on first access."""
+
+    def __init__(self, names):
+        self.available = frozenset(names)
+        self.loaded = []
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        if name not in self.available:
+            raise AttributeError(f"DSA has no attribute {name!r}")
+        self.loaded.append(name)
+        _decorate_like_cutlass_dsl_4_6()
+
+        def entry_point(*args, **kwargs):
+            return None
+
+        setattr(self, name, entry_point)
+        return entry_point
+
+
+class _Activation:
+    """Stands for a tensor that is live on the Python stack."""
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def manual_gc():
+    enabled = gc.isenabled()
+    gc.disable()
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        if enabled:
+            gc.enable()
+
+
+def _install(monkeypatch, namespace):
+    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "cudnn", types.SimpleNamespace(DSA=namespace))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_cudnn_dsa", None)
+    return namespace
+
+
+def test_namespace_resolves_every_entry_point_once(monkeypatch):
+    namespace = _install(monkeypatch, _LazyDSANamespace(dsa_cudnn_kernels._CUDNN_DSA_ENTRY_POINTS))
+    dsa_cudnn_kernels._ensure_dsa_namespace()
+    dsa_cudnn_kernels._ensure_dsa_namespace()
+    assert dsa_cudnn_kernels._cudnn_dsa is namespace
+    assert sorted(namespace.loaded) == sorted(dsa_cudnn_kernels._CUDNN_DSA_ENTRY_POINTS)
+
+
+def test_entry_point_missing_from_the_frontend_is_left_to_its_call_site(monkeypatch):
+    available = set(dsa_cudnn_kernels._CUDNN_DSA_ENTRY_POINTS) - {"SparseAttentionBackward"}
+    namespace = _install(monkeypatch, _LazyDSANamespace(available))
+    dsa_cudnn_kernels._ensure_dsa_namespace()
+    assert dsa_cudnn_kernels._cudnn_dsa is namespace
+    assert getattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels._cudnn_dsa, "SparseAttentionBackward", None) is None
+
+
+def test_lazy_frontend_model_pins_the_caller_without_a_collection(manual_gc):
+    """Positive control: the modelled frontend leaks exactly like the real one."""
+    namespace = _LazyDSANamespace(["sparse_attention_backward_wrapper"])
+
+    def backward_step():
+        activation = _Activation()
+        _ = namespace.sparse_attention_backward_wrapper
+        return weakref.ref(activation)
+
+    activation = backward_step()
+    assert activation() is not None
+    gc.collect()
+    assert activation() is None
+
+
+def test_first_use_inside_a_step_does_not_pin_the_step(monkeypatch, manual_gc):
+    _install(monkeypatch, _LazyDSANamespace(dsa_cudnn_kernels._CUDNN_DSA_ENTRY_POINTS))
+
+    def backward_step():
+        activation = _Activation()
+        dsa_cudnn_kernels._ensure_dsa_namespace()
+        dsa_cudnn_kernels._cudnn_dsa.sparse_attention_backward_wrapper()
+        return weakref.ref(activation)
+
+    assert backward_step()() is None
+
+
+def test_entry_point_list_covers_every_namespace_access():
+    source = inspect.getsource(dsa_cudnn_kernels)
+    used = set(re.findall(r"_cudnn_dsa\.([A-Za-z_]\w*)", source))
+    used |= set(re.findall(r"getattr\(\s*_cudnn_dsa,\s*\"([A-Za-z_]\w*)\"", source))
+    assert used
+    assert used <= set(dsa_cudnn_kernels._CUDNN_DSA_ENTRY_POINTS)

+"""``dsa_indexer_skip_masked_score_fill`` on an MLA ``DSAttention`` layer (real kernels).
+
+With the switch on, the cuDNN packed-THD indexer scorer is called with ``clean_logits=False``
+and leaves every score column at or past a row's causal limit unspecified. The unspecified
+columns are additionally poisoned (NaN, +inf) through a caller-owned score buffer, which is
+the worst case a reader past the limit could observe. Each layout runs in two modes:
+
+* deterministic mode: a full forward/backward of the layer must be bitwise identical to the
+  run with the ``-inf`` prefill: top-k indices, attention output, indexer loss and every
+  gradient.
+* production (non-deterministic) mode: the radix top-k writes its selection in an
+  unspecified slot order and the sparse backward accumulates with atomics, so two prefilled
+  runs already differ. Each row's top-k index set, sorted by key index, and the score of
+  every selected key must still be exactly equal; the output, indexer loss and gradients
+  must agree within a tolerance that the prefilled rerun itself has to meet.
+
+Layouts follow packed THD training: multi-sequence packs with a dummy tail sequence and
+fixed-capacity ``cu_seqlens`` (``thd_max_packed_sequences``), at CP1 and zigzag CP4, and
+dynamic-CP static slots where a microbatch runs on a CP2 or CP1 subgroup of a CP4 world with
+one real sequence plus the dummy tail. The metadata is produced by ``pad_sequence_for_thd``,
+the same helper the data path uses. Run with 4 ranks.
+"""
+
+import dataclasses
+import functools
+import math
+from typing import Optional
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state
+from megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine import TELinear, TENorm
+from megatron.core.packed_seq_params import PackedSeqParams, pad_sequence_for_thd
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupCollection
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed
+from megatron.core.transformer.enums import AttnBackend, AttnMaskType
+from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant import dsa_cudnn_kernels
+from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant.dsa import (
+    DSAIndexer,
+    DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler,
+    DSAIndexerLossLoggingHelper,
+    DSAIndexerSubmodules,
+    DSAttention,
+    DSAttentionSubmodules,
+)
+from megatron.core.transformer.spec_utils import ModuleSpec
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import MLATransformerConfig
+from megatron.core.utils import init_method_normal, scaled_init_method_normal
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils

+_WORLD_SIZE = 4

+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _Layout:
+    """One packed THD microbatch as every rank of the realized CP group sees it."""
+
+    model_cp: int  # CP size the model parallel state is initialized with
+    realized_cp: int  # CP size of the group that runs this microbatch
+    dynamic: bool  # realized group is a dynamic-CP subgroup (local_cp_size/cp_group set)
+    local_rows: int  # static per-rank slot length (pad target)
+    seq_lens: tuple  # real sequences; the dummy tail fills the slot
+    max_num_seqs: int  # thd_max_packed_sequences, including the dummy sequence
+    topk: int
+
+
+_LAYOUTS = [
+    pytest.param(_Layout(1, 1, False, 512, (200, 120, 136), 5, 128), id="cp1-3seq-dummy"),
+    # topk == max_seqlen_k: the scorer's full-cover shortcut instead of the ranked top-k.
+    pytest.param(_Layout(1, 1, False, 256, (152, 64), 4, 256), id="cp1-2seq-dummy-fullcover"),
+    pytest.param(_Layout(4, 4, False, 256, (416, 336, 160), 5, 128), id="cp4-3seq-dummy"),

+def _skip_unless_supported() -> None:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required for the cuDNN DSA backend")
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10:
+        pytest.skip("the cuDNN frontend clean_logits scorer path needs SM100+")
+    if Utils.world_size != _WORLD_SIZE:

+    try:

+    dsa_cudnn_kernels._ensure_dsa_namespace()

+def _make_config(layout: _Layout, *, deterministic: bool) -> MLATransformerConfig:
+    """64-head DSA attention geometry (512+64 latent, 32x128 indexer), small hidden."""
+    config = MLATransformerConfig(
+        multi_latent_attention=True,
+        experimental_attention_variant="dsa",
+        num_layers=4,
+        hidden_size=2048,

+        output_layer_init_method=scaled_init_method_normal(0.02, 1, multiplier=2.0),
+        use_cpu_initialization=False,

+def _make_attention(config: MLATransformerConfig, pg_collection: ProcessGroupCollection):
+    indexer_spec = ModuleSpec(
+        module=DSAIndexer,
+        submodules=DSAIndexerSubmodules(
+            linear_wq_b=ModuleSpec(module=TELinear),

+def _packed_seq_params(layout: _Layout, cp_group, cp_rank: int) -> PackedSeqParams:
+    """Static-slot THD metadata exactly as ``pad_sequence_for_thd`` emits it."""
+    lengths = torch.tensor((0, *layout.seq_lens), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    cu_seqlens = lengths.cumsum(0, dtype=torch.int32)
+    real_rows = int(cu_seqlens[-1])
+    assert real_rows % layout.realized_cp == 0
+    params = PackedSeqParams(
+        qkv_format="thd",
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_kv=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_q_padded=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_kv_padded=cu_seqlens,
+        max_seqlen_q=max(layout.seq_lens),
+        max_seqlen_kv=max(layout.seq_lens),
+        local_cp_size=layout.realized_cp if layout.dynamic else None,
+        cp_group=cp_group if layout.dynamic else None,
+        cp_partition_mode="zigzag",
+    )
+    tokens = torch.zeros((1, real_rows // layout.realized_cp), dtype=torch.long, device="cuda")
+    padded = pad_sequence_for_thd(
+        tokens,
+        None,
+        None,
+        None,
+        params,
+        target_len=layout.local_rows,
+        max_num_seqs=layout.max_num_seqs,
+        tail_padding_policy="append_dummy_seq",
+        cp_size=layout.realized_cp,
+        cp_rank=cp_rank,
+    )[4]
+    global_rows = layout.local_rows * layout.realized_cp
+    expected = [0, *torch.tensor(layout.seq_lens).cumsum(0).tolist(), global_rows]
+    expected += [global_rows] * (layout.max_num_seqs + 1 - len(expected))
+    assert padded.cu_seqlens_q.tolist() == expected, padded.cu_seqlens_q.tolist()
+    assert padded.max_seqlen_q == padded.max_seqlen_kv == global_rows
+    if layout.dynamic:
+        assert padded.local_cp_size == layout.realized_cp and padded.cp_group is cp_group
+    return padded
+

+def _make_inputs(config: MLATransformerConfig, layout: _Layout, rank: int) -> dict:
+    """Rank-local absorbed-MLA query/key and indexer activations for this slot."""
+    rows = layout.local_rows
+    heads = config.num_attention_heads
+    absorbed_dim = config.kv_lora_rank + config.qk_pos_emb_head_dim
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
+    generator.manual_seed(2026 + rank)
+
+    def randn(*shape, scale=1.0):
+        return torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator) * scale
+
+    return {
+        "query": randn(rows, 1, heads, absorbed_dim),
+        "key": randn(rows, 1, 1, absorbed_dim),
+        "x": randn(rows, 1, config.hidden_size, scale=8.0),
+        "qr": randn(rows, 1, config.q_lora_rank, scale=8.0),
+        "up_v_weight": randn(heads, config.v_head_dim, config.kv_lora_rank),
+    }
+
+
+class _ScorerSpy:
+    """Proxy for the cuDNN DSA namespace that records ``clean_logits`` and can poison.
+
+    With a poison value, every ``clean_logits=False`` indexer call gets a caller-owned
+    score buffer prefilled with that value, so each column the kernel leaves unwritten
+    reads back as the poison.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, namespace):
+        self._namespace = namespace
+        self.poison: Optional[float] = None
+        self.clean_logits_calls = []
+        self.poison_visible = []
+        real = namespace.indexer_forward_wrapper
+
+        @functools.wraps(real)
+        def indexer_forward_wrapper(q, k, w, *args, **kwargs):
+            clean_logits = kwargs.get("clean_logits", True)
+            self.clean_logits_calls.append(clean_logits)
+            if clean_logits or self.poison is None:
+                return real(q, k, w, *args, **kwargs)
+            assert not args and kwargs.get("out") is None and q.ndim == 3, "THD scorer expected"
+            columns = int(kwargs["max_seqlen_k"])
+            # An unaligned caller buffer is staged by the frontend; keep the layouts aligned.
+            assert columns % 4 == 0, f"max_seqlen_k={columns} must be a multiple of 4"
+            kwargs["out"] = torch.full(
+                (q.size(0), columns), self.poison, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device
+            )
+            result = real(q, k, w, *args, **kwargs)
+            scores = result["scores"]
+            assert scores.data_ptr() == kwargs["out"].data_ptr()
+            hit = torch.isnan(scores) if math.isnan(self.poison) else scores == self.poison
+            self.poison_visible.append(bool(hit.any()))
+            return result
+
+        self.indexer_forward_wrapper = indexer_forward_wrapper
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        return getattr(self._namespace, name)
+
+
+def _step(attention, inputs, packed_seq_params, topk_log, *, skip_fill: bool):
+    """One forward/backward of the layer; returns top-k, output, indexer loss and grads."""
+    attention.config.dsa_indexer_skip_masked_score_fill = skip_fill
+    DSAIndexerLossLoggingHelper.clean_loss_in_tracker()
+    attention.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+    topk_log.clear()
+    # The indexer reads x and qr detached (its loss trains only the indexer), so only the
+    # attention operands are leaves; the indexer gradients are checked on its parameters.
+    leaves = {
+        name: inputs[name].detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+        for name in ("query", "key", "up_v_weight")
+    }
+    output = attention(
+        query=leaves["query"],
+        key=leaves["key"],
+        value=None,
+        attention_mask=None,
+        x=inputs["x"],
+        qr=inputs["qr"],
+        attn_mask_type=AttnMaskType.causal,
+        packed_seq_params=packed_seq_params,
+        up_v_weight=leaves["up_v_weight"],
+    )
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
+    generator.manual_seed(7 + torch.distributed.get_rank())
+    grad_output = torch.randn(output.shape, device="cuda", dtype=output.dtype, generator=generator)
+    output.backward(grad_output)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    result = {"output": output.detach(), "indexer_loss": None}
+    result["indexer_loss"] = DSAIndexerLossLoggingHelper.tracker["values"][0].detach().clone()
+    for call, returned in enumerate(topk_log):
+        for position, tensor in enumerate(returned):
+            if tensor is not None:
+                result[f"topk.call{call}.{position}"] = tensor
+    for name, leaf in leaves.items():
+        assert leaf.grad is not None, f"input {name} has no gradient"
+        result[f"grad.{name}"] = leaf.grad.detach().clone()
+    for name, parameter in attention.named_parameters():
+        assert parameter.grad is not None, f"parameter {name} has no gradient"
+        result[f"grad.{name}"] = parameter.grad.detach().clone()
+    return result
+
+
+# Production-mode tolerances. The top-k slot order changes the accumulation order of the
+# sparse attention, and the sparse backward reduces with atomics, so two identical runs
+# differ by a few bf16 ulps. A wrong or poisoned selection moves whole rows by O(1).
+_PRODUCTION_REL_L2 = 1e-2  # ||actual - expected|| / ||expected|| per tensor
+_PRODUCTION_PEAK = 2e-2  # max |actual - expected| / max |expected| per tensor
+_PRODUCTION_LOSS_RTOL = 1e-3  # the indexer loss is an fp32 scalar
+
+
+def _bitwise_equal(value: torch.Tensor, reference: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    return torch.equal(value.reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8), reference.reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8))
+
+
+def _assert_bitwise_equal(actual: dict, expected: dict, label: str) -> None:
+    assert actual.keys() == expected.keys(), f"{label}: {sorted(actual)} != {sorted(expected)}"
+    for name, reference in expected.items():
+        value = actual[name]
+        assert value.dtype == reference.dtype and value.shape == reference.shape, (
+            f"{label} {name}: {value.dtype}{tuple(value.shape)} != "
+            f"{reference.dtype}{tuple(reference.shape)}"
+        )
+        if not _bitwise_equal(value, reference):
+            diff = (value.double() - reference.double()).abs()
+            pytest.fail(
+                f"{label}: {name} differs bitwise in "
+                f"{int((value != reference).sum())}/{value.numel()} elements "
+                f"(max |diff| {diff.nan_to_num(nan=float('inf')).max().item():.3e})"
+            )
+
+
+def _is_topk_indices(name: str) -> bool:
+    return name.startswith("topk.") and name.endswith(".0")
+
+
+def _sort_topk_by_key(result: dict) -> dict:
+    """Sort each row's top-k selection by key index and carry the selected scores along.
+
+    Without deterministic mode the cuDNN radix top-k writes its selection in an
+    unspecified slot order. The selected set, its length and the score of every selected
+    key are still reproducible. Invalid slots (``-1``) sort last.
+    """
+    canonical = dict(result)
+    for name, indices in result.items():
+        if not _is_topk_indices(name):
+            continue
+        invalid = torch.full_like(indices, torch.iinfo(indices.dtype).max)
+        order = torch.where(indices >= 0, indices, invalid).argsort(dim=-1, stable=True)
+        canonical[name] = torch.gather(indices, -1, order)
+        scores_name = name.rsplit(".", 1)[0] + ".2"
+        if scores_name in result:
+            scores = result[scores_name]
+            assert scores.shape == indices.shape, f"{scores_name} is not a top-k score payload"
+            canonical[scores_name] = torch.gather(scores, -1, order)
+    return canonical
+
+
+def _slot_order_diffs(actual: dict, expected: dict) -> int:
+    """Raw top-k slots that differ, i.e. how much the unspecified slot order moved."""
+    return sum(
+        int((actual[name] != expected[name]).sum()) for name in expected if _is_topk_indices(name)
+    )
+
+
+def _ratio(numerator: torch.Tensor, denominator: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    numerator, denominator = float(numerator), float(denominator)
+    if denominator > 0:
+        return numerator / denominator
+    return 0.0 if numerator == 0 else math.inf
+
+
+def _production_mismatches(actual: dict, expected: dict, label: str):
+    """Compare two production-mode runs whose top-k selections are sorted by key.
+
+    Top-k indices, lengths and scores must be bitwise equal. Every other tensor must be
+    finite and within the production tolerances. Returns the failures and, per compared
+    tensor, ``(relative L2 error, peak error relative to the peak magnitude)``.
+    """
+    if actual.keys() != expected.keys():
+        return [f"{label}: {sorted(actual)} != {sorted(expected)}"], {}
+    failures, errors = [], {}
+    for name, reference in expected.items():
+        value = actual[name]
+        if value.dtype != reference.dtype or value.shape != reference.shape:
+            failures.append(
+                f"{label} {name}: {value.dtype}{tuple(value.shape)} != "
+                f"{reference.dtype}{tuple(reference.shape)}"
+            )
+            continue
+        if name.startswith("topk."):
+            if not _bitwise_equal(value, reference):
+                failures.append(
+                    f"{label}: sorted {name} differs in "
+                    f"{int((value != reference).sum())}/{value.numel()} elements"
+                )
+            continue
+        value64, reference64 = value.double(), reference.double()
+        if not (torch.isfinite(value64).all() and torch.isfinite(reference64).all()):
+            failures.append(f"{label}: {name} has non-finite values")
+            continue
+        diff = (value64 - reference64).abs()
+        rel_l2 = _ratio(diff.norm(), reference64.norm())
+        peak = _ratio(diff.max(), reference64.abs().max())
+        errors[name] = (rel_l2, peak)
+        if name == "indexer_loss":
+            limits = (_PRODUCTION_LOSS_RTOL, _PRODUCTION_LOSS_RTOL)
+        else:
+            limits = (_PRODUCTION_REL_L2, _PRODUCTION_PEAK)
+        if rel_l2 > limits[0] or peak > limits[1]:
+            failures.append(
+                f"{label}: {name} rel L2 {rel_l2:.3e} (limit {limits[0]:.0e}), "
+                f"peak {peak:.3e} (limit {limits[1]:.0e})"
+            )
+    return failures, errors
+
+
+def _worst(errors: dict) -> str:
+    if not errors:
+        return "no float tensors"
+    l2_name = max(errors, key=lambda name: errors[name][0])
+    peak_name = max(errors, key=lambda name: errors[name][1])
+    loss = errors.get("indexer_loss", (math.nan,))[0]
+    return (
+        f"max rel L2 {errors[l2_name][0]:.2e} ({l2_name}), "
+        f"max peak {errors[peak_name][1]:.2e} ({peak_name}), loss rel {loss:.2e}"
+    )
+

+def _initialize_model_parallel(layout: _Layout) -> None:
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(

+        context_parallel_size=layout.model_cp,
+        dynamic_context_parallel=layout.dynamic,

+
+def _build_step(layout: _Layout, monkeypatch, *, deterministic: bool):
+    """Build the layer and inputs for ``layout``; returns the step function and scorer spy.
+
+    The model parallel state must already be initialized for ``layout``.
+    """
+    model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(1234)
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)

+    pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups(required_pgs=["tp", "cp"])

+        pg_collection.cp = parallel_state.get_dynamic_data_context_parallel_groups(
+            group_size=layout.realized_cp
+        )
+    cp_group = pg_collection.cp
+    assert cp_group.size() == layout.realized_cp
+    config = _make_config(layout, deterministic=deterministic)
+    attention = _make_attention(config, pg_collection)
+    packed_seq_params = _packed_seq_params(layout, cp_group, cp_group.rank())
+    inputs = _make_inputs(config, layout, torch.distributed.get_rank())
+
+    spy = _ScorerSpy(dsa_cudnn_kernels._cudnn_dsa)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_cudnn_dsa", spy)
+    topk_log = []
+    indexer_topk = dsa_cudnn_kernels._indexer_topk_bshd
+
+    def recording_indexer_topk(*args, **kwargs):
+        returned = indexer_topk(*args, **kwargs)
+        topk_log.append(tuple(None if t is None else t.detach().clone() for t in returned))
+        return returned
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_indexer_topk_bshd", recording_indexer_topk)
+    return functools.partial(_step, attention, inputs, packed_seq_params, topk_log), spy

+def _run_skipped(step, spy, poison: Optional[float]) -> dict:
+    """One step with the prefill skipped and the unspecified columns poisoned."""
+    spy.poison = poison

+    spy.poison_visible.clear()

+
+_POISONS = (None, float("nan"), float("inf"))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", _LAYOUTS)

+"""Deterministic DSA top-k from cuDNN ``tie_break=1`` versus the full-row canonical rule.
+
+``RadixTopK`` models the cuDNN frontend radix top-k on CPU: scores are ranked by the
+frontend's ordered radix key (bit pattern, so ``+0.0`` ranks above ``-0.0``), ``tie_break``
+0 picks random copies of the cutoff key, 1 the lowest columns, rows no longer than K return
+``0..len-1`` then ``-1``, and the output order is shuffled (the kernel does not sort).
+"""

+import logging
+import weakref

+import pytest
+import torch

+from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant import dsa_cudnn_kernels
+
+_INT64_MAX = torch.iinfo(torch.int64).max
+
+
+def _radix_keys(scores: torch.Tensor, nan_mode: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """cuDNN ``to_ordered`` key for FP32 scores; smaller keys rank higher."""
+    bits = scores.contiguous().view(torch.int32).to(torch.int64) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    keys = torch.where(bits >= 0x80000000, bits, (~bits) & 0x7FFFFFFF)
+    if nan_mode == "top":
+        # Another legal NaN placement: every NaN above every number (fp16 coarse bins).
+        keys = torch.where(torch.isnan(scores), torch.full_like(keys, -1), keys)
+    else:
+        assert nan_mode == "bits"
+    return keys
+
+
+class RadixTopK:
+    """CPU model of ``cudnn.DSA.indexer_top_k_wrapper`` (frontend 1.31 signature)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, seed: int = 0, nan_mode: str = "bits"):
+        self.generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+        self.nan_mode = nan_mode
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def indexer_top_k_wrapper(
+        self,
+        input_values,
+        seq_lens,
+        top_k,
+        next_n=1,
+        return_val=True,
+        num_copy_bits=256,
+        stream=None,
+        tie_break=0,
+    ):
+        assert next_n == 1 and tie_break in (0, 1)
+        self.calls.append(
+            {
+                "rows": input_values.size(0),
+                "tie_break": tie_break,
+                "val": return_val,
+                "offset_bytes": input_values.storage_offset() * input_values.element_size(),
+            }
+        )
+        n_rows, sk = input_values.shape
+        keys = _radix_keys(input_values, self.nan_mode)
+        if tie_break == 1:
+            tie_rank = torch.arange(sk, dtype=torch.int64).expand(n_rows, sk)
+        else:
+            tie_rank = torch.argsort(torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=self.generator), dim=1)
+        lengths = seq_lens.to(torch.int64).view(n_rows, 1)
+        columns = torch.arange(sk).view(1, sk)
+        composite = torch.where(columns < lengths, keys * sk + tie_rank, _INT64_MAX)
+        indices = torch.argsort(composite, dim=1)[:, :top_k].to(torch.int32)
+        shuffle = torch.argsort(torch.rand((n_rows, top_k), generator=self.generator), dim=1)
+        indices = torch.gather(indices, 1, shuffle)
+        trivial = lengths.view(n_rows) <= top_k
+        prefix = torch.arange(top_k, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, top_k)
+        prefix = torch.where(prefix < lengths, prefix, torch.full_like(prefix, -1))
+        indices = torch.where(trivial.view(n_rows, 1), prefix, indices)
+        values = None
+        if return_val:
+            values = torch.gather(input_values, 1, indices.clamp(min=0).to(torch.int64))
+            values = torch.where(indices >= 0, values, torch.full_like(values, float("-inf")))
+        return {"indices": indices, "values": values}
+

+def _random_rows(seed: int, distribution: str, n_rows: int = 48, sk: int = 96):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    if distribution == "gauss":
+        scores = torch.randn((n_rows, sk), generator=generator)

+    elif distribution == "signed_zeros":

+        choices = torch.tensor([0.0, -0.0, 0.25, -0.5, 1.0])
+        weights = torch.tensor([10.0, 10.0, 1.0, 3.0, 1.0])
+        picks = torch.multinomial(weights, n_rows * sk, replacement=True, generator=generator)
+        scores = choices[picks].view(n_rows, sk)
+    elif distribution == "relu_heads":
+        # DSA index score sum_h w_h * relu(q_h . k), accumulated from the first head's term:
+        # rows whose head weights are all negative score -0.0 wherever every logit is <= 0.
+        heads = 4
+        logits = torch.round(torch.randn((n_rows, heads, sk), generator=generator) * 2) / 2
+        exact_negative_zero = torch.rand((n_rows, heads, sk), generator=generator) < 0.1
+        logits = torch.where(exact_negative_zero, torch.full_like(logits, -0.0), logits)
+        weights = torch.randn((n_rows, heads, 1), generator=generator).sign() * 0.5
+        weights[::2] = -weights[::2].abs()
+        terms = torch.relu(logits) * weights
+        scores = terms[:, 0]
+        for head in range(1, heads):
+            scores = scores + terms[:, head]
+    elif distribution == "denormal_zeros":
+        # Zeros of both signs next to +-denormals: denormals must never count as zero ties.
+        tiny = torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny

+        scores = choices[picks].view(n_rows, sk)

+    elif distribution == "specials":

+        scores = choices[picks].view(n_rows, sk)

+    scores = scores.to(torch.float32).contiguous()

+    columns = torch.arange(sk).view(1, sk)
+    garbage = torch.where(
+        torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator) < 0.5,
+        torch.full((n_rows, sk), float("nan")),
+        torch.full((n_rows, sk), -0.0),
+    )
+    scores = torch.where(columns < seq_lens.view(n_rows, 1), scores, garbage)
+    return scores, seq_lens

+def _sort_reference(scores, seq_lens, topk_k):
+    """Independent rule: drop NaN and -inf, take the top in-row scores by value with the
+    lowest index first among equal values (so -0.0 ties +0.0), minus one slot per positive
+    NaN the radix kernel ranks into the top K, then sort by index; pad -1 / finfo.min."""
+    n_rows, sk = scores.shape
+    columns = torch.arange(sk).view(1, sk)
+    in_row = columns < seq_lens.view(n_rows, 1).long()
+    selectable = in_row & (scores > float("-inf"))
+    keyed = torch.where(selectable, scores + 0.0, torch.full_like(scores, float("-inf")))
+    order = torch.sort(keyed, dim=1, descending=True, stable=True).indices
+    positive_nan = in_row & torch.isnan(scores) & (_bits(scores) >= 0)
+    long_row = seq_lens.long() > topk_k
+    budget = torch.where(
+        long_row, topk_k - positive_nan.sum(dim=1).clamp(max=topk_k), selectable.sum(dim=1)
+    )
+    budget = torch.minimum(budget, selectable.sum(dim=1))
+    keep = torch.arange(sk).view(1, sk) < budget.view(n_rows, 1)
+    chosen = torch.sort(torch.where(keep, order, sk), dim=1).values[:, :topk_k]
+    indices = torch.where(chosen == sk, -1, chosen).to(torch.int32)
+    values = torch.gather(scores, 1, indices.clamp(min=0).long())
+    values = torch.where(indices >= 0, values, torch.finfo(torch.float32).min)
+    return {"indices": indices, "values": values}

+def test_positive_infinity_is_selected_and_nan_slots_stay_empty(canonicalize):
+    """+inf/NaN rows: a rule that drops +inf members returns the +inf rows count-short.
+
+    +inf is the largest score and must be selected (by both the ``tie_break=1`` derivation and
+    the full-row rule it reproduces); a NaN still costs the slot the kernel ranked it into.
+    """
+    sk, topk_k = 64, 16
+    scores = torch.randn((6, sk), generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(5))

+    scores[1, 10] = float("nan")  # NaN inside the row: one slot short, by rule
+    scores[2, [3, 9]] = float("inf")
+    scores[2, 20] = float("nan")
+    scores[3, :] = float("inf")  # more +inf than K: the lowest-index copies
+    scores[4, :8] = float("inf")  # short row (len <= K) of +inf and finite scores
+    scores[5, [1, 2]] = float("-inf")  # -inf is the mask value and is never selected

+    assert counts == [topk_k, topk_k - 1, topk_k - 1, topk_k, 12, topk_k]
+    assert {0, sk // 7, sk // 3, sk // 2, sk - 1} <= set(actual["indices"][0].tolist())

+class _ReleaseTracker:
+    """Weak references to every chunk-level tensor; all must be dead at the next launch."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.refs = []
+        self.launches = 0
+
+    def track(self, result):
+        for tensor in (result["indices"], result["values"]):
+            if tensor is not None:
+                self.refs.append(weakref.ref(tensor))
+        return result
+
+    def assert_released(self):
+        alive = sum(ref() is not None for ref in self.refs)
+        assert alive == 0, f"{alive} chunk tensors are still alive at launch {self.launches}"
+        self.launches += 1
+

+"""Real cuDNN frontend checks of the DSA top-k chunking and deterministic tie-break path.
+
+Run on one SM90+ GPU with the installed frontend:
+
+* FE >= 1.31 (``tie_break``): the deterministic wrapper (``tie_break=1`` + index sort +
+  zero-tie repair) must equal the full-row canonical rule bitwise, indices and value bits,
+  on Gaussian, heavy-tie, signed-zero (mixed ``-0.0``/``+0.0`` at the cutoff, all-zero rows),
+  NaN/infinity, short and garbage-tailed rows, at row widths that take the kernel's 16-bit,
+  32-bit shared-memory and global-spill paths; it must repeat bitwise and give the same result
+  from a CUDA graph replay as eagerly.
+* FE < 1.31 (no ``tie_break``): the probe must report no support and the wrapper must fall
+  back to the full-row rule.
+* Both: with an 8 GiB scratch budget (set by the tests; the default is 2 GiB), 1M-column
+  chunks of 1024 rows (exactly 2**31 scratch elements) select the right set, and the scratch
+  peak stays within the budget; eagerly and in a CUDA graph's private pool the chunked call
+  reserves one scratch block, not one per launch.
+* FE >= 1.31: ``tie_break=1`` and ``return_val=False`` reach the real frontend, and 1M-column
+  rows whose cutoff is a signed zero (every row) match the full-row rule.
+
+Lines starting with ``[topk-gpu]`` report timings and memory for the validation log.
+"""

+import time
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant import (
+    dsa_cudnn_kernels,
+    dsa_topk_zero_ties,
+)
+
+_GIB = 1024**3
+
+
+def _use_8gib_scratch_budget(monkeypatch):
+    """1024 rows per launch at 1M columns: exactly the frontend's 2**31 scratch elements."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_TOPK_WRAPPER_MAX_SCRATCH_BYTES", 8 * _GIB)
+
+
+def _require_frontend():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is required")
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 9:
+        pytest.skip("cuDNN radix top-k needs SM90+")
+    try:
+        from cudnn import DSA  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        pytest.skip("cuDNN frontend DSA is not installed")
+    dsa_cudnn_kernels._ensure_dsa_namespace()
+
+
+def _require_tie_break():
+    _require_frontend()
+    if not dsa_cudnn_kernels._supports_lowest_index_topk_tie_break():
+        pytest.skip(
+            f"cuDNN frontend {dsa_cudnn_kernels._cudnn_frontend_version()} has no tie_break"
+        )
+
+
+def _report(message: str) -> None:
+    print(f"[topk-gpu] {message}", flush=True)
+
+
+def _bits(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return values.contiguous().view(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _assert_bitwise_equal(actual: dict, expected: dict, label: str) -> None:
+    mismatched_rows = (actual["indices"] != expected["indices"]).any(dim=1)
+    assert not bool(mismatched_rows.any()), (
+        f"{label}: {int(mismatched_rows.sum())} rows differ in indices, first rows "
+        f"{torch.nonzero(mismatched_rows).view(-1)[:8].tolist()}"
+    )
+    if expected["values"] is None:
+        assert actual["values"] is None
+        return
+    value_rows = (_bits(actual["values"]) != _bits(expected["values"])).any(dim=1)
+    assert not bool(value_rows.any()), f"{label}: {int(value_rows.sum())} rows differ in values"
+
+
+def _full_row_rule(scores, seq_lens, topk_k, return_topk_scores, monkeypatch):
+    """Today's deterministic path: raw tie_break=0 top-k plus the full-row canonicalization."""
+    with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+        patch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_supports_lowest_index_topk_tie_break", lambda: False)
+        return dsa_cudnn_kernels._indexer_top_k_wrapper_chunked(
+            scores, seq_lens, topk_k, return_topk_scores, deterministic=True
+        )
+
+
+def _tie_break_path(scores, seq_lens, topk_k, return_topk_scores):
+    return dsa_cudnn_kernels._indexer_top_k_wrapper_chunked(
+        scores, seq_lens, topk_k, return_topk_scores, deterministic=True
+    )
+
+
+def _lengths(n_rows, sk, topk_k, generator):
+    lengths = torch.randint(topk_k + 1, sk + 1, (n_rows,), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+    # Short rows (len <= K, including 0 and exactly K) take the kernel's trivial path.
+    short = torch.tensor([0, 1, topk_k - 1, topk_k, topk_k + 1, sk], device="cuda")
+    lengths[: short.numel()] = short.clamp(max=sk)
+    return lengths.to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _make_rows(kind: str, n_rows: int, sk: int, topk_k: int, seed: int):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    seq_lens = _lengths(n_rows, sk, topk_k, generator)

+    elif kind == "heavy_ties":
+        # 1/64-rounded scores: hundreds to thousands of copies of the cutoff value.
+        scores = torch.round(torch.randn((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda") * 4)
+        scores = scores / 64
+    elif kind == "signed_zeros":
+        # Fewer than K positives, then zeros of random sign: the cutoff is +-0 in most rows.
+        uniform = torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+        positives = torch.randint(0, topk_k, (n_rows, 1), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+        rank = torch.argsort(uniform, dim=1).argsort(dim=1)
+        sign = torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda") < 0.5
+        zeros = torch.where(sign, torch.zeros_like(uniform), torch.full_like(uniform, -0.0))
+        negatives = -uniform - 0.01
+        scores = torch.where(rank < positives, uniform + 0.01, zeros)
+        third = sk // 3
+        scores = torch.where(rank >= sk - third, negatives, scores)
+    elif kind == "denormal_zeros":
+        # Fewer than K positives, then zeros of both signs mixed with +-denormals: denormals
+        # are not zeros (no flush to zero), so they must never fill zero-tie slots.
+        uniform = torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+        tiny = torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny
+        positives = uniform < (topk_k / 2) / sk
+        scores = torch.where(
+            uniform < 0.5, torch.full_like(uniform, 0.0), torch.full_like(uniform, -0.0)
+        )
+        pick = torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+        scores = torch.where(pick < 0.02, torch.full_like(scores, tiny / 4), scores)
+        scores = torch.where(
+            (pick >= 0.02) & (pick < 0.04), torch.full_like(scores, -tiny / 4), scores
+        )
+        scores = torch.where(
+            (pick >= 0.04) & (pick < 0.05), torch.full_like(scores, tiny / 1024), scores
+        )
+        scores = torch.where(pick >= 0.7, -uniform - 0.01, scores)
+        scores = torch.where(positives, uniform + 0.01, scores)
+        assert bool(((scores != 0) & (scores.abs() < tiny)).any()), "denormals were flushed"
+    elif kind == "all_zeros":
+        sign = torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda") < 0.5
+        scores = torch.where(
+            sign,
+            torch.zeros((n_rows, sk), device="cuda"),
+            torch.full((n_rows, sk), -0.0, device="cuda"),
+        )
+        scores[0::3] = 0.0
+        scores[1::3] = -0.0
+    elif kind == "specials":
+        scores = torch.round(torch.randn((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda") * 2) / 4
+        pick = torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+        scores = torch.where(pick < 0.002, torch.full_like(scores, float("nan")), scores)
+        scores = torch.where(
+            (pick >= 0.002) & (pick < 0.004), torch.full_like(scores, -float("nan")), scores
+        )
+        scores = torch.where(
+            (pick >= 0.004) & (pick < 0.005), torch.full_like(scores, float("inf")), scores
+        )
+        scores = torch.where(
+            (pick >= 0.005) & (pick < 0.05), torch.full_like(scores, -float("inf")), scores
+        )
+        scores = torch.where((pick >= 0.05) & (pick < 0.2), torch.full_like(scores, -0.0), scores)
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError(kind)
+    # Columns past a row's length are undefined with clean_logits=False: poison them.
+    columns = torch.arange(sk, device="cuda").view(1, sk)
+    poison = torch.where(
+        torch.rand((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda") < 0.5,
+        torch.full((n_rows, sk), float("nan"), device="cuda"),
+        torch.full((n_rows, sk), 1.0e30, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    scores = torch.where(columns < seq_lens.view(n_rows, 1).long(), scores, poison)
+    return scores.float().contiguous(), seq_lens
+
+
+# (n_rows, sk): 16-bit column indices, 32-bit indices in shared memory, global spill.
+_WIDTHS = [(96, 8192), (64, 70000), (24, 300000)]
+_KINDS = ["gauss", "heavy_ties", "signed_zeros", "denormal_zeros", "all_zeros", "specials"]
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", _KINDS)

+    scores, seq_lens = _make_rows(kind, n_rows, sk, topk_k, seed=seed)

+    expected = _full_row_rule(scores, seq_lens, topk_k, True, monkeypatch)
+    actual = _tie_break_path(scores, seq_lens, topk_k, True)
+    indices_only = _tie_break_path(scores, seq_lens, topk_k, False)

+    _assert_bitwise_equal(actual, expected, f"{kind} {n_rows}x{sk} k={topk_k}")

+def test_tie_break_path_keeps_lowest_index_ties_against_a_sort_reference():

+    scores, seq_lens = _make_rows("heavy_ties", n_rows, sk, topk_k, seed=17)
+    zeros = _make_rows("signed_zeros", n_rows, sk, topk_k, seed=18)
+    scores = torch.cat((scores, zeros[0]))
+    seq_lens = torch.cat((seq_lens, zeros[1]))
+    columns = torch.arange(sk, device="cuda").view(1, sk)
+    masked = torch.where(columns < seq_lens.view(-1, 1).long(), scores, float("-inf"))
+    # Adding +0.0 turns -0.0 into +0.0, so the stable sort sees value ties (whatever its
+    # float key order) and keeps them in index order.
+    masked = masked + 0.0
+    order = torch.sort(masked, dim=1, descending=True, stable=True).indices[:, :topk_k]
+    keep = torch.arange(topk_k, device="cuda").view(1, -1) < seq_lens.view(-1, 1).clamp(max=topk_k)
+    reference = torch.sort(torch.where(keep, order, sk), dim=1).values
+    reference = torch.where(reference == sk, -1, reference).to(torch.int32)
+
+    actual = _tie_break_path(scores, seq_lens, topk_k, True)
+
+    assert torch.equal(actual["indices"], reference)
+    gathered = torch.gather(scores, 1, actual["indices"].clamp(min=0).long())
+    valid = actual["indices"] >= 0
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(actual["values"])[valid], _bits(gathered)[valid])

+def _inf_nan_rows(n_rows, sk, seed):
+    """The NaN/inf row plan: per 8-row block NaN at 1000 / past the end / clean /
+    at 10 / at L-1 / at L//2, five +inf with no NaN, NaN at 0."""
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    scores = torch.randn((n_rows, sk), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+    seq_lens = torch.randint(sk - sk // 8, sk + 1, (n_rows,), generator=generator, device="cuda")
+    seq_lens = seq_lens.to(torch.int32)
+    seq_lens[1::8] = sk - 1
+    lengths = seq_lens.tolist()
+    for row in range(n_rows):
+        length = lengths[row]
+        plan = row % 8
+        if plan == 0:
+            scores[row, min(1000, length - 1)] = float("nan")
+        elif plan == 1:
+            scores[row, length] = float("nan")
+        elif plan == 3:
+            scores[row, min(10, length - 1)] = float("nan")
+        elif plan == 4:
+            scores[row, length - 1] = float("nan")
+        elif plan == 5:
+            scores[row, length // 2] = float("nan")
+        elif plan == 6:
+            scores[row, sorted({0, length // 7, length // 3, length // 2, length - 1})] = float(
+                "inf"

+        elif plan == 7:
+            scores[row, 0] = float("nan")

+    budget = torch.where(nan_rows, topk_k - 1, topk_k).view(-1, 1)
+    reference = torch.where(

+class _FrontendSpy:
+    """Records the real frontend's top-k calls; its signature names ``tie_break``."""

+    def __init__(self, namespace):

+        self.calls = []

+    def indexer_top_k_wrapper(
+        self, input_values, seq_lens, top_k, next_n=1, return_val=True, tie_break=0
+    ):
+        self.calls.append((int(input_values.size(0)), bool(return_val), int(tie_break)))
+        return self.namespace.indexer_top_k_wrapper(
+            input_values,
+            seq_lens,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            next_n=next_n,
+            return_val=return_val,

+    assert spy.calls and all(tie_break == 0 for _, _, tie_break in spy.calls)
+    spy.calls.clear()

+# ------------------------------------------------------------------- G10 payload bound
+def _recompute_row_sum(e):
+    """The cuDNN FE 1.31 recompute's FP32 row sum of ``e`` (``[rows, 2048]``, indexer epilogue).
+
+    Thread ``lane`` of warp ``w`` holds slots ``32 w + lane + 128 i`` (i = 0..15) and sums them
+    in that order; a 32-lane xor butterfly sums each warp; the 4 warp sums are added in turn.
+    """
+    rows = e.size(0)
+    per_thread = e.view(rows, 16, 4, 32)
+    acc = torch.zeros(rows, 4, 32)
+    for slot in range(16):
+        acc = acc + per_thread[:, slot]
+    lanes = torch.arange(32)
+    for offset in (16, 8, 4, 2, 1):
+        acc = acc + acc[:, :, lanes ^ offset]
+    warps = acc[:, :, 0]
+    return ((warps[:, 0] + warps[:, 1]) + warps[:, 2]) + warps[:, 3]
+
+
+def _recompute_payload(logits, row_sum=_recompute_row_sum):
+    """``log(max(p, FLT_MIN))`` with ``p = exp2((s - max) log2 e) * (1 / sum)``, all in FP32."""
+    e = torch.exp2((logits - logits.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values) * math.log2(math.e))
+    p = e * (1.0 / row_sum(e)).unsqueeze(-1)
+    return torch.log(p.clamp_min(_FLT_MIN))

+def _contributions(case, generator):
+    """``[2 ranks, adds, 2 * _ROWS_PER_RANK key rows, D]`` FP32 dKV contributions."""
+    shape = (2, _ADDS, 2 * _ROWS_PER_RANK, _D)
+    if case == "coherent":
+        return torch.rand(shape, generator=generator) * 2.7
+    if case == "mixed":
+        return torch.randn(shape, generator=generator) * 3 + 0.5
+    if case == "zero-mean":
+        return torch.randn(shape, generator=generator) * 3
+    if case == "wide":
+        return torch.randn(shape, generator=generator) * torch.logspace(-6, 1, _D)
+    # Large partials of opposite signs on the two ranks: dkey is about 0.
+    base = torch.randn(shape[1:], generator=generator) * 10
+    noise = 1 + 1e-3 * torch.randn(shape[1:], generator=generator)
+    return torch.stack([base, -base * noise])

+def _atomic_partials(contributions, generator):
+    """Each rank's BF16 partial: its FP32 sum of the adds in a random (atomic) order."""
+    partials = []
+    for per_rank in contributions:
+        total = torch.zeros(per_rank.shape[1:])
+        for add in torch.randperm(per_rank.size(0), generator=generator).tolist():
+            total = total + per_rank[add]
+        partials.append(total.bfloat16())
+    return torch.stack(partials)
+

+def _reduce_scatter(partials, rank):
+    """Rank ``rank``'s dkey: the 2-rank BF16 reduce-scatter of its rows (one rounding)."""
+    rows = slice(rank * _ROWS_PER_RANK, (rank + 1) * _ROWS_PER_RANK)
+    return (partials[0, rows].float() + partials[1, rows].float()).bfloat16()

+        got = _reduce_scatter(replay, rank) if replay_dkey is None else replay_dkey[rank]
+        want = _reduce_scatter(eager, rank)

+"""``dsa_indexer_scorer_backend='deepgemm'`` on ``DSAttention`` layers (real kernels).
+
+Needs SM 10.3 GPUs (SM 10.0 with ``MCORE_DEEPGEMM_VALIDATE_SM100=1``), a ``deep_gemm >= 2.8``
+build, Transformer Engine MXFP8, the cuDNN frontend DSA (>= 1.29, else the scorer falls back)
+and FlashMLA; each test states its rank count. The layers run the cuDNN fused DSA path with ``dsa_indexer_precision='mxfp8'``:
+
+* checkpoint replay with the indexer loss (``dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`` off and on,
+  1 rank): the replay that re-selects and the replay that reuses the first call's stash give
+  the same output, loss and gradients, so the first call (indices only) and the replay (with
+  scores) score bitwise-identical logits, and the stash protocol takes the BF16-recompute
+  payload. Every run selects through a pinned top-k (the first call's selection, checked
+  against each later call's logits): cuDNN's BF16 radix top-k does not repeat its choice
+  among tied logits, which is why the config requires the reuse for a recompute that replays
+  the indexer;
+* frozen indexer (loss off, 1 rank, the same pinned top-k): eager, replay-rerun and
+  replay-reuse agree;
+* production mode against the cuDNN MXFP8 scorer (4 ranks; CP1, zigzag CP4 and dynamic-CP
+  layouts of the skip-fill layer test, plus a wide CP4 layout where DeepSelect takes the BF16
+  top-k): DeepGEMM ran with no fallback, both scorers fed the indexer loss the FP32
+  recompute (the rule follows the MXFP8 precision, not the backend), the selections overlap,
+  the indexer loss and gradients track, and a rerun selects nearly the same keys (overlap
+  >= 0.999: cuDNN's BF16 radix top-k may keep other tied keys; the kernel-level behaviour,
+  bitwise repeats for DeepSelect and tie-only differences for cuDNN, is checked in
+  ``test_dsa_deepgemm_scorer_gpu.py``);
+* CUDA graph capture/replay of a CP2 layer fed by the prebuilt packed-CP layout tables (2
+  ranks): DeepGEMM ran inside the capture; after an in-place refresh to another packing too,
+  the replay scores bitwise the logits eager scored and its own cuDNN BF16 radix selection
+  equals eager's tie-aware (with no key taken twice); given eager's selection (fed through
+  buffers allocated before the capture) its output, dquery and dup_v_weight equal eager's
+  bitwise. dkey, which cuDNN's sparse-attention backward sums with FP32 atomics, is checked per
+  element: each rank's dkey partial (the gradient at the key's CP all-gather) within that
+  summation order's bound, each run's dkey as one BF16 rounding of the summed partials, and
+  dkey within the partials' differences. The captured step runs with
+  ``set_sync_debug_mode('error')``. Every check is collected and raised on both ranks at the
+  next synchronization point, before any rank enters a captured collective, and the graph is
+  released before the process groups go.
+
+Every test warms DeepGEMM up after model-parallel init has set the rank's device (DeepGEMM
+runs on one device per process), and the 1-rank tests alias the padded cu_seqlens of Q and K
+as the THD schedulers do (the MXFP8 scorer needs that proof).
+
+Lines starting with ``[deepgemm-layer]`` report what each rank compared.

+class _PinnedTopk:
+    """Every DeepGEMM-path top-k of a test returns the selection of its first call.
+
+    The runs below select on bitwise-identical DeepGEMM logits, but cuDNN's BF16 radix top-k
+    does not repeat its choice among tied BF16 logits (seen on GB300; the reason the
+    config requires ``dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`` for a recompute that replays the
+    indexer). Pinning the selection lets the checkpoint and stash protocols compare
+    bitwise; every later call checks that its logits equal the first call's on each in-row
+    column, so the pin never hides a scoring difference.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch):
+        self.calls = 0
+        self.first = None
+        real = dsa_cudnn_kernels._deepgemm_logits_topk
+
+        def pinned(logits, lengths, topk_k, topk_backend, topk_scratch_bytes=None):
+            self.calls += 1
+            columns = torch.arange(logits.size(1), device=logits.device).view(1, -1)
+            seen = torch.where(
+                columns < lengths.view(-1, 1).long(), logits, torch.zeros_like(logits)
+            )
+            if self.first is None:
+                indices, values = real(logits, lengths, topk_k, topk_backend, topk_scratch_bytes)
+                self.first = (seen.clone(), lengths.clone(), indices.clone(), values.clone())
+                return indices, values
+            first_seen, first_lengths, indices, values = self.first
+            assert torch.equal(lengths, first_lengths), "the pinned top-k saw other row lengths"
+            assert torch.equal(seen, first_seen), "the pinned top-k saw other logits"
+            return indices.clone(), values.clone()
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_deepgemm_logits_topk", pinned)
+

+class _GraphTopkRecorder:
+    """Records every DeepGEMM-path top-k; inside a capture it feeds the layer a static selection.
+
+    cuDNN's BF16 radix top-k does not repeat its choice among tied BF16 logits (G5's documented
+    negative), so an eager step and a graph replay of the same inputs may keep other keys tied
+    at a row's K-th value, and on this layer one swapped key moves the output and gradients by
+    far more than the comparison tolerance. Outside capture the real selection passes through
+    and the in-row logits, lengths, indices and values are recorded (cloned). Inside capture
+    the real top-k still runs and its in-row logits, lengths and selection are kept in static
+    tensors that every replay refreshes, but the layer gets ``pinned``, buffers the test
+    fills with the matching eager step's selection before each replay. So a replay is checked
+    three ways: its logits bitwise against eager's, its own selection tie-aware against eager's,
+    and its output and gradients against eager's given eager's selection.
+
+    ``pinned`` is allocated before the capture (``allocate_pinned``) and never inside it: a
+    capture allocation comes from the graph's private pool, which hands out memory that
+    tensors freed earlier in the same capture used, so every replay rewrites it before the
+    layer reads it (seen on GB300: after a replay the pinned indices read 0 in
+    12131-14592 of 16384 slots, and the output was off by up to 135).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch):
+        self.eager = []
+        self.captured = None
+        self.pinned = None
+        real = dsa_cudnn_kernels._deepgemm_logits_topk
+
+        def recorded(logits, lengths, topk_k, topk_backend, topk_scratch_bytes=None):
+            indices, values = real(logits, lengths, topk_k, topk_backend, topk_scratch_bytes)
+            columns = torch.arange(logits.size(1), device=logits.device).view(1, -1)
+            seen = torch.where(
+                columns < lengths.view(-1, 1).long(), logits, torch.zeros_like(logits)
+            )
+            if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+                assert self.captured is None, "one DeepGEMM top-k per captured step"
+                assert self.pinned is not None, "allocate the pinned selection before the capture"
+                for pinned, produced in zip(self.pinned, (indices, values)):
+                    assert (pinned.shape, pinned.dtype) == (produced.shape, produced.dtype), (
+                        f"pinned {tuple(pinned.shape)} {pinned.dtype}, the top-k gave "
+                        f"{tuple(produced.shape)} {produced.dtype}"
+                    )
+                self.captured = (seen, lengths.clone(), indices, values)
+                return self.pinned
+            self.eager.append((seen.clone(), lengths.clone(), indices.clone(), values.clone()))
+            return indices, values
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(dsa_cudnn_kernels, "_deepgemm_logits_topk", recorded)
+
+    def take_eager(self):
+        """The one selection the last eager step recorded."""
+        assert len(self.eager) == 1, f"{len(self.eager)} DeepGEMM top-k calls in one step"
+        return self.eager.pop()
+
+    def allocate_pinned(self, selection) -> None:
+        """Allocate the layer's static selection, shaped like ``selection``, before the capture."""
+        assert not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing(), "allocate pinned before the capture"
+        self.pinned = tuple(torch.empty_like(source) for source in selection[2:])
+
+    def pin(self, selection) -> None:
+        """Feed the next replays ``selection`` (an eager record) as the layer's top-k."""
+        for target, source in zip(self.pinned, selection[2:]):
+            assert target.shape == source.shape, (tuple(target.shape), tuple(source.shape))
+            target.copy_(source)
+
+    def compare_replay(self, selection, label) -> int:
+        """The replay's logits bitwise and its own selection tie-aware against ``selection``.
+
+        Returns the number of rows whose replay selection kept other keys (tied ones only).
+        """
+        seen, lengths, indices, _values = self.captured
+        want_seen, want_lengths, want_indices, _ = selection

+        differ = seen.view(torch.int16) != want_seen.view(torch.int16)

+            f"{label}: the replay scored other logits on {int(differ.sum())} in-row elements, "
+            f"max |diff| {(seen.float() - want_seen.float()).abs().max().item():.3e}"

+        counts, want_counts = (indices >= 0).sum(dim=-1), (want_indices >= 0).sum(dim=-1)
+        assert torch.equal(counts, want_counts), (
+            f"{label}: {int((counts != want_counts).sum())} of {counts.numel()} rows selected "
+            "another number of keys"
+        )
+        # The value multisets below cannot tell one tied key taken twice from two tied keys.
+        valid_slots = lengths.clamp(max=indices.size(-1))
+        for name, chosen in (("replay", indices), ("eager", want_indices)):
+            repeated = _repeated_key_rows(chosen, valid_slots)
+            assert not repeated, f"{label}: {repeated} rows of the {name} selection repeat a key"
+
+        def selected(chosen):
+            values = torch.gather(seen.float(), 1, chosen.long().clamp(min=0))
+            return torch.where(chosen >= 0, values, float("-inf")).sort(dim=-1).values
+
+        assert torch.equal(
+            selected(indices), selected(want_indices)
+        ), f"{label}: the replay selected keys that are not ties at a row's cutoff"
+        keys, want_keys = indices.sort(dim=-1).values, want_indices.sort(dim=-1).values
+        return int((keys != want_keys).any(dim=-1).sum())
+
+
+def _repeated_key_rows(indices, valid_slots) -> int:
+    """Rows of ``indices`` (``[rows, K]``) whose valid slots name some key twice.
+
+    A slot is valid below ``valid_slots[row]`` and when its index is not negative. A tie-aware
+    comparison compares the selected values as a multiset, which a top-k that took one tied
+    key twice instead of two tied keys would pass; this check does not.
+    """
+    slots = torch.arange(indices.size(-1), device=indices.device).view(1, -1)
+    valid = (slots < valid_slots.view(-1, 1).long()) & (indices >= 0)
+    keys = torch.where(valid, indices.long(), -1).sort(dim=-1).values
+    return int(((keys[:, 1:] == keys[:, :-1]) & (keys[:, 1:] >= 0)).any(dim=-1).sum())
+
+
+class _KeyPartials:
+    """Records this rank's dkey partial: the gradient at the layer's CP all-gather of the key.
+
+    The gathered key (rank-major rows) is permuted into the global key order and read by
+    cuDNN's sparse attention, whose backward returns dKV in BF16 from an FP32 atomic
+    accumulator; the permutation's backward gathers it back exactly. So the hooked gradient is
+    that BF16 dKV in gathered order, the inverse key reorder included, and the gather's
+    backward, a BF16 CP reduce-scatter, sums the ranks' partials into each rank's dkey: rank r
+    gets the gathered rows ``[r * _GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS, (r + 1) * _GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS)``. Outside
+    capture each step appends a copy to ``eager``; inside capture ``captured`` is a static copy
+    that every replay refreshes.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, monkeypatch, key_dim: int):
+        self.eager = []
+        self.captured = None
+        real = dsa.gather_from_sequence_parallel_region
+
+        def gather(input_, *args, **kwargs):
+            output = real(input_, *args, **kwargs)
+            if (
+                output.requires_grad
+                and output.size(0) == _GRAPH_GLOBAL_ROWS
+                and output.size(-1) == key_dim
+            ):
+                output.register_hook(self._record)
+            return output
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(dsa, "gather_from_sequence_parallel_region", gather)
+
+    def _record(self, grad) -> None:
+        partial = grad.detach().clone()
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            assert self.captured is None, "one key gather per captured step"
+            self.captured = partial
+        else:
+            self.eager.append(partial)
+
+    def take_eager(self):
+        """The partial the last eager step recorded."""
+        assert len(self.eager) == 1, f"{len(self.eager)} key gathers in one step"
+        return self.eager.pop()
+
+
+def _bf16_ulp(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Spacing of BF16 numbers at ``|values|``: ``2**(floor(log2|v|) - 7)``, and ``2**-133``
+    (the subnormal spacing) below ``2**-126``, zero included. Built from the exponent bits, so
+    it is exact on any device."""
+    magnitude = values.float().abs()
+    power = (magnitude.view(torch.int32) & 0x7F800000).view(torch.float32)
+    return torch.where(
+        magnitude < 2.0**-126, torch.full_like(magnitude, 2.0**-133), power * 2.0**-7
+    )
+
+
+# FP32 reorder term of a dkey partial element. cuDNN's backward (FE 1.31 dsa_bwd_sm100) runs one
+# CTA per (query row, block of 64 heads) and atomically adds its FP32 dKV tile, so with 64 heads an
+# element takes at most one add per local query row (_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS = 256). Two orders of n
+# adds differ by at most 2 gamma_(n-1) sum|c| < 2**-15 sum|c| here. Assumed, not proven: the
+# contributions to each element of a key row add up in magnitude to at most 64 times that row's
+# largest |partial| M_row, so the term is at most 2**-9 M_row.
+_PARTIAL_REORDER_PER_ROW_SCALE = 2.0**-9
+
+
+def _partial_order_bound(replay, eager):
+    """Elementwise bound on ``|replay - eager|`` for one rank's dkey partial (``[rows, ..., D]``).
+
+    Both are the BF16 rounding of an FP32 sum of the same contributions in two atomic orders:
+    ``|bf16(s) - bf16(s')| <= |s - s'| + (ulp(s) + ulp(s')) / 2``, each ulp at most that of the
+    larger BF16 result, and ``|s - s'|`` at most ``_PARTIAL_REORDER_PER_ROW_SCALE`` times the
+    largest ``|partial|`` of either run in that key row.
+    """
+    larger = torch.maximum(replay.float().abs(), eager.float().abs())
+    row_scale = larger.reshape(larger.size(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
+    row_scale = row_scale.view(-1, *([1] * (larger.dim() - 1)))
+    return _bf16_ulp(larger) + _PARTIAL_REORDER_PER_ROW_SCALE * row_scale
+
+
+def _reduce_scatter_bound(dkey, summed):
+    """Bound on ``|dkey - summed|`` within one run, ``summed`` the FP32 sum of the partials.
+
+    The reduce-scatter of two ranks rounds the sum of two BF16 partials to BF16 once: half a
+    BF16 ulp. ``summed`` is exact unless the partials' exponents differ by more than 16, and a
+    sum taken through FP32 first rounds twice; ``2**-16`` ulp covers both.
+    """
+    assert _GRAPH_CP == 2, "one rounding models the reduce-scatter of two ranks only"
+    larger = torch.maximum(dkey.float().abs(), summed.abs())
+    return _bf16_ulp(larger) * (0.5 + 2.0**-16)
+
+
+def _dkey_bound(replay, eager, partial_diff):
+    """Bound on ``|replay - eager|`` for this rank's dkey rows, given ``partial_diff``: the summed
+    ``|replay - eager|`` of every rank's partial on those rows. Each run's dkey lies within
+    ``_reduce_scatter_bound`` of its summed partials."""
+    larger = torch.maximum(replay.float().abs(), eager.float().abs())
+    return partial_diff + _bf16_ulp(larger) * (1 + 2.0**-15)
+
+
+def _bounded_mismatch(actual, expected, bound, label):
+    """(failure or ``None``, statistics) for ``|actual - expected| <= bound`` elementwise.
+
+    A non-finite value on either side fails.
+    """
+    diff = (actual.float() - expected.float()).abs()
+    over = ~(diff <= bound) | ~torch.isfinite(actual) | ~torch.isfinite(expected)
+    stats = (
+        f"{label} {int((diff > 0).sum())}/{diff.numel()} differ, max |diff| "
+        f"{diff.max().item():.3e}, max |diff|/bound {(diff / bound).max().item():.3f}"
+    )
+    if bool(over.any()):
+        return f"{label}: {int(over.sum())} elements past the bound; {stats}", stats
+    return None, stats
+
+
+def _mismatch(actual, expected, label):
+    """``None`` when ``actual`` equals ``expected`` exactly, else the mismatch statistics."""
+    if actual.shape != expected.shape or actual.dtype != expected.dtype:
+        return (
+            f"{label}: {tuple(actual.shape)} {actual.dtype} against "
+            f"{tuple(expected.shape)} {expected.dtype}"
+        )
+    if torch.equal(actual, expected):
+        return None
+    diff = (actual.float() - expected.float()).abs()
+    return (
+        f"{label}: {int((actual != expected).sum())} of {actual.numel()} elements differ, max "
+        f"|diff| {diff.max().item():.3e}, max |expected| {expected.float().abs().max().item():.3e}"
+    )
+
+
+class _CollectedFailures:
+    """The graph test's failed checks, raised on every rank of ``group`` at once.
+
+    A rank that raised alone would leave the others waiting in their next collective, a captured
+    one inside a replay included (the original "F, then a hang"). So the test collects every
+    check and raises only at its synchronization points, where all ranks reduce the count.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, group, device="cuda"):
+        self.group = group
+        self.device = device
+        self.messages = []
+        self.cause = None
+
+    def add(self, message) -> None:
+        """Collect ``message`` unless it is ``None``."""
+        if message:
+            self.messages.append(message)
+
+    def check(self, condition, message) -> None:
+        """Collect ``message`` when ``condition`` is false."""
+        if not condition:
+            self.messages.append(message)
+
+    def run(self, check, *args):
+        """``check(*args)``, with an AssertionError collected (then ``None`` is returned)."""
+        try:
+            return check(*args)
+        except AssertionError as error:
+            self.messages.append(str(error) or repr(error))
+            self.cause = self.cause or error
+            return None
+
+    def raise_on_any_rank(self, where) -> None:
+        """A collective: raise on every rank when any rank collected a failure."""
+        count = torch.tensor([len(self.messages)], dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device)
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(count, group=self.group)
+        total = int(count.item())
+        if total:
+            here = "; ".join(self.messages) if self.messages else "none"
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"{where}: {total} failed checks on the CP ranks; on this rank: {here}"
+            ) from self.cause
+
+

+    config.dsa_indexer_precision = "mxfp8"
+    config.dsa_indexer_scorer_backend = backend

+def _overlap(actual: dict, expected: dict) -> list:
+    """Per top-k call: mean |A ∩ B| / |B| over rows, with equal lengths required."""
+    means = []
+    for name in sorted(n for n in expected if layer_helpers._is_topk_indices(n)):
+        call = name.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
+        lengths = expected[f"{call}.1"].reshape(-1)
+        assert torch.equal(actual[f"{call}.1"].reshape(-1), lengths), f"{call} lengths differ"
+        a = actual[name].reshape(lengths.numel(), -1).long()
+        b = expected[name].reshape(lengths.numel(), -1).long()
+        keys = int(max(a.max(), b.max())) + 2
+        member = torch.zeros((a.size(0), keys), dtype=torch.bool, device=a.device)
+        member.scatter_(1, torch.where(b >= 0, b, keys - 1), True)
+        member[:, keys - 1] = False
+        hits = torch.gather(member, 1, torch.where(a >= 0, a, keys - 1)).sum(dim=1)
+        keep = lengths > 0
+        means.append((hits[keep].float() / lengths[keep].float()).mean().item())
+    return means
+

+# -------------------------------------------------------- CUDA graph with prebuilt layout (2 ranks)
+_GRAPH_CP = 2
+_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS = 256
+_GRAPH_GLOBAL_ROWS = _GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS * _GRAPH_CP
+_PACK_A = (0, 128, 384, _GRAPH_GLOBAL_ROWS)
+_PACK_B = (0, 256, 256, _GRAPH_GLOBAL_ROWS)
+_GRAD_INPUTS = ("query", "key", "up_v_weight")
+
+
+def _graph_params(boundaries, cp_group) -> PackedSeqParams:
+    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(boundaries, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    params = PackedSeqParams(
+        qkv_format="thd",
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_kv=cu_seqlens,
+        max_seqlen_q=_GRAPH_GLOBAL_ROWS,
+        max_seqlen_kv=_GRAPH_GLOBAL_ROWS,
+        cp_group=cp_group,
+    )
+    prebuild_thd_cp_partition_routes(params, cp_group)
+    assert prebuild_packed_cp_layout(params) is not None
+    return params
+
+
+def _graph_inputs(config, seed):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    absorbed_dim = config.kv_lora_rank + config.qk_pos_emb_head_dim
+
+    def randn(*shape, scale=1.0):
+        return torch.randn(*shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator) * scale
+
+    heads = config.num_attention_heads
+    return {
+        "query": randn(_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS, 1, heads, absorbed_dim),
+        "key": randn(_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS, 1, 1, absorbed_dim),
+        "x": randn(_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS, 1, config.hidden_size, scale=8.0),
+        "qr": randn(_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS, 1, config.q_lora_rank, scale=8.0),
+        "up_v_weight": randn(heads, config.v_head_dim, config.kv_lora_rank),
+        "grad_output": randn(_GRAPH_LOCAL_ROWS, 1, heads * config.v_head_dim),
+    }
+
+
+def _graph_step(attention, inputs, params):
+    output = attention(
+        query=inputs["query"],
+        key=inputs["key"],
+        value=None,
+        attention_mask=None,
+        x=inputs["x"],
+        qr=inputs["qr"],
+        attn_mask_type=AttnMaskType.causal,
+        packed_seq_params=params,
+        up_v_weight=inputs["up_v_weight"],
+    )
+    output.backward(inputs["grad_output"].view_as(output))
+    return output
+
+
+def _graph_eager(attention, inputs, params):
+    leaves = {name: value.detach().clone() for name, value in inputs.items()}
+    for name in _GRAD_INPUTS:
+        leaves[name].requires_grad_(True)
+    output = _graph_step(attention, leaves, params)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return output.detach().clone(), {name: leaves[name].grad.clone() for name in _GRAD_INPUTS}
+

+def _deep_gemm_calls_fail(dg, monkeypatch):
+    """Make every deep_gemm function raise and record its name (restore with the return)."""
+    called = []

+        name: getattr(dg.dg, name)
+        for name in ("get_num_sms", "get_mqa_logits_metadata", "fp8_fp4_mqa_logits")

+        return call

+    for name in originals:

+
+    def restore():
+        for name, function in originals.items():
+            monkeypatch.setattr(dg.dg, name, function)

+    return called, restore

+def _bf16_reference_log_probs(q, k, w, indices, lengths):
+    """FP32 log-softmax over each row's selected keys of the BF16 dense logits."""
+    q32, k32, w32 = q[0].float(), k[0].float(), w[0].float()
+    dense = (torch.einsum("thd,kd->thk", q32, k32).relu() * w32.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=1)
+    valid = torch.arange(indices.size(-1)).view(1, 1, -1) < lengths.unsqueeze(-1)
+    gathered = torch.gather(dense, 1, indices[0].clamp(min=0).long()).unsqueeze(0)
+    return dsa_masking.masked_log_softmax(gathered, valid), valid
+

+"""Real-kernel checks of ``dsa_indexer_scorer_backend='deepgemm'`` (single GPU).
+
+Needs a ``deep_gemm >= 2.8`` build, SM 10.3 (SM 10.0 when ``MCORE_DEEPGEMM_VALIDATE_SM100=1``,
+which is how a GB200 run validates it), Transformer Engine MXFP8 and the cuDNN frontend DSA
+namespace at >= 1.29 (older frontends keep the cuDNN MXFP8 scorer); DeepSelect is used where
+installed. CP>1 layouts run on one GPU: the scorer needs only this rank's local query rows and
+the globally ordered packed keys. Every DeepGEMM-scored call checks that DeepGEMM really ran
+(no logged fallback reason, a logits launch), so a silent fallback cannot pass. Covered:
+
+* G1 the output contract: BF16, 1024-byte rows, a full-row view inside the allocation, values
+  against a dequantized reference;
+* G2 exact mapping on ternary inputs (bitwise against integer math) for CP1 packs, zigzag CP2
+  and CP4 ranks, unequal segments, uncovered tail rows (CP1) and a query block straddling the
+  covered boundary; nothing is written outside ``[ks, ke)``, checked on a poisoned block the
+  caching allocator must hand back (the test fails if it does not); tie-aware selection
+  equality with the FE BF16 scorer;
+* G3 Gaussian and outlier selection against FE MXFP8 (overlap) and FE BF16 (recall);
+* G4 CUDA graph capture/replay equal to eager (tie-aware on the DeepGEMM logits for cuDNN's
+  top-k), no host sync, and the capture guard in a fresh process, raised before any
+  deep_gemm call, both by a direct ``mqa_logits`` and by the production entry point
+  (``_deepgemm_scorer_fallback_reason``, which reaches ``jit_problem``) with no device claimed
+  (the subprocess prints any exception's type and text);
+* G5 repeatability, batch independence and indices-only against value calls (a layer
+  recomputed without ``dsa_indexer_reuse_checkpoint_topk`` selects again in its replay):
+  bitwise for DeepSelect BF16; for cuDNN's BF16 radix top-k a documented negative, tie-aware
+  only (it keeps other tied keys on a repeat, which is why the config requires the reuse for
+  a recompute that replays the indexer);
+* G6 NaN in a K row and a Q row (records whether the logits are NaN and their sign);
+* G7, the selected-score recompute against log-softmax of FE BF16 scores, lives in
+  ``test_dsa_cudnn_mxfp8_scorer_gpu.py`` with the recompute itself: it is the loss rule of
+  every MXFP8 scorer, not of DeepGEMM;
+* G8 the sparse indexer loss and gradients equal the BF16 path's given the same selection,
+  plus the cost of using DeepGEMM's own BF16 values instead (report only);
+* G9 cuDNN's BF16 radix top-k on DeepGEMM-shaped logits at 4K..1M widths: exact, never past a
+  row's length (lengths not a multiple of 16), repeatable up to ties (bitwise reported);
+* G10 calls of more rows than one DeepGEMM call takes: row chunks select what one call
+  selects (bitwise for DeepSelect, tie-aware for cuDNN) and feed the loss the same payload
+  (bitwise where the slots match; where cuDNN returned the same keys in another slot order,
+  which reorders the recompute's FP32 row sum, within that order's absolute bound on
+  ``log p``, ``_log_prob_order_bound``), and 65536 rows with 64 heads (past the 58104-row
+  limit and TE's 65535-row MXFP8 cast of Q) run in two calls.
+
+Every tie-aware comparison (equal multisets of selected values) also requires each row's
+valid slots to name distinct keys, which a multiset of values cannot show.
+
+Lines starting with ``[deepgemm-gpu]`` report what was measured.
